items.title: PlayStation 2
items.line: The PlayStation 2 launched in Japan on 4 March 2000, North America on 26 October at $299 and Europe on 24 November. It played DVDs, and sales passed 155 million.

items.title: The Sims
items.line: The Sims came out on 4 February 2000. Will Wright's virtual dollhouse passed Myst as the best-selling PC game, with over 6.3 million sold by March 2002.

items.title: Tate Modern opens
items.line: Tate Modern opened on 11 May 2000 in the old Bankside Power Station on the Thames, converted by Herzog & de Meuron. It drew 5.25 million visitors in its first year.

items.title: Big Brother
items.line: Big Brother began on Channel 4 on 18 July 2000. Davina McCall presented, and Craig Phillips won after 64 days in the house.

items.title: Euro 2000
items.line: Euro 2000, co-hosted by Belgium and the Netherlands, ran from 10 June to 2 July. France beat Italy 2-1 in the final with a David Trezeguet golden goal.

items.title: The Millennium Dome
items.line: The Millennium Dome opened on 1 January 2000 after a New Year's Eve party with the Queen. About 6.5 million came, half the 12 million forecast, and the total bill hit £789 million.

items.title: Gladiator
items.line: Gladiator opened in the US on 5 May 2000. Ridley Scott's film won five Oscars, including Best Picture and Best Actor for Russell Crowe, on a $103 million budget.
